//: Tracked HIGH/CRITICAL npm-audit advisory exceptions for client/desktop. Consumed by scripts/security/npm-audit-gate.{sh,mjs} via the build.yml 'Dependency audit' step. PREFER bumping the dependency (an `overrides` entry in package.json) over accepting. Only add an entry here when no fixed version exists yet. Each entry: { "id": "GHSA-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx", "package": "<npm package the advisory was reported for>", "reason": "why accepted + tracking link", "review_by": "YYYY-MM-DD", "scope": "dev" (optional) }. `package` is REQUIRED and is matched against what npm reported — an entry without it, or scoped to a different package, does NOT suppress and blocks instead, because a bare GHSA id is a standing waiver far broader than any reviewed reason (advisories are amended in place, and a package can move onto a runtime path under the same id). `scope: dev` is VERIFIED against a production-only `npm audit --omit=dev` report, not taken on trust, and fails closed when that report is unavailable. An expired review_by emits a CI warning (never a block). See [internal]quality-gate-definition.md 'npm-audit gate'.

accepted.reason: image-size ICNS parser DoS (infinite loop) — packaging-time only, and no fixed version exists on any line (vulnerable <= 2.0.2, first-patched NONE). Reached solely via @electron-forge/maker-dmg@7.11.2 -> electron-installer-dmg@5.0.1 -> appdmg@0.6.6 -> image-size@0.7.5, which the lockfile marks dev+optional; appdmg declares ^0.7.4 and 0.7.5 is the newest published release, and appdmg is effectively unmaintained — so no override can reach a patched version because none has been published on any line. Reach is narrow but NOT the icon: appdmg's 'Reading background dimensions' step (lib/appdmg.js:289) calls sizeOf on opts.background, the DMG background image; the .icns is fs.copyFile'd at ~:303 and never parsed. Note image-size routes by MAGIC BYTES, not file extension, so any file handed to background is content-sniffed — a file named .png whose first bytes are 'icns' reaches this parser. The vulnerable ICNS loop is genuinely present in 0.7.5. Bounded because the only CI job that reaches it (pr-smoke-build in build-desktop.yml) already runs PR-controlled code by design — npm ci executes scripts/patch-electron-plist.sh as postinstall — with contents:read, persist-credentials:false and no secrets, so a crafted background buys an attacker strictly less than they already have. Never runs at application runtime; never bundled into renderer or main. Tracked: https://github.com/Concord-Voice/Concord-Voice-Alpha/issues/2727

extract-zip unvalidated symlink path traversal — no fixed version exists on any line (vulnerable <= 2.0.1, first-patched NONE; 2.0.1 is the newest published release), so an acceptance is the only available action. Build-time only, reached solely via @electron-forge/cli@7.11.2 -> @electron-forge/core@7.11.2 -> @electron/packager@18.4.4 -> extract-zip@2.0.1; the lockfile marks it dev, and it is absent from a production-only audit, so it never runs at application runtime and is never bundled into renderer or main. What @electron/packager extracts with it are the Electron release archives it downloads from Electron's own CDN and integrity-checks before extraction, so the traversal needs a malicious archive at that step. The scope:dev claim above is re-verified by the gate against `npm audit --omit=dev` on every run, so this entry self-invalidates if extract-zip ever becomes runtime-reachable. Tracked: https://github.com/Concord-Voice/Concord-Voice-Alpha/issues/2734

image-size JXL and HEIF parser DoS (infinite loops) — INAPPLICABLE to the resolved version, not merely unreachable: image-size@0.7.5 ships no jxl.js and no heif.js (its lib/types/ is bmp, cur, dds, gif, icns, ico, jpg, png, psd, svg, tiff, webp), so the vulnerable code does not exist here. The advisory's <= 2.0.2 range is over-broad and catches 0.7.5 anyway, and there is no published fix on any line to bump to, so an acceptance is the only available action. Same dev+optional packaging chain as GHSA-W3RX-R6R6-PGPR above. Re-check this if image-size is ever bumped INTO a version that does ship those parsers. Tracked: https://github.com/Concord-Voice/Concord-Voice-Alpha/issues/2727
